notes.title: Yomi and Puzzle Strike are 70% off during the Steam Digital Tabletop Fest!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8668643/00b66642c57ccff70f8d71fff383f412ac5569b5.png[/img]

Board Game Night is back with the [b]Steam Digital Tabletop Fest![/b]

From [b]October 21st until October 26th[/b] you can save [b]70%[/b] on our digital versions of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/287960/Yomi/]Yomi[/url] (our fighting-game-in-card-form), [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/386740/Puzzle_Strike/]Puzzle Strike[/url] (a competitive deckbuilding game with high interaction) and their DLCs.

Interested in more tabletop goodness? Check out David Sirlin’s [url=https://www.patreon.com/sirlin]Patreon[/url] page, where about twice a month we’re giving our Patrons a behind-the-scenes look at the two tabletop games we’re working on right now! If you’re a longtime fan of [b]Yomi[/b] and [b]Puzzle Strike[/b], the Patreon is the best way to support us while also gaining access to some awesome new content. 

It’s great that we can still get together for board games over the internet, even when we can’t be together in person. Be sure to support your favorite indie developers during the sale and we’ll see you all online!

Stay safe everyone!

notes.title: 2016-02-16 update
notes.notes:
Here are the patch notes for today's Yomi update:

- Replays manipulation UI (Public / Private toggle, Keep checkbox, Delete button), just like webplayer Yomi (and Steam Puzzle Strike) already had
- New speed status reminders, in yellow "speed boxes" on the playfield to remind you of some speed-altering conditions.
-- Gwen's Chillbane and Vendetta's Acrobatics: "+2.0 slower"
-- Lum's Roll the Dice J,Q,K: "+4.0 slower"
-- Rook's Entangling Vines: "-3.0, min 1.0"
-- Zane's Meaty Attacks (when the opponent is KD): "1.0 normals"
-- Vendetta's Wall Dive Loop (when the opponent is KD): "1.0 King"
-- BBB's Long Range: "1.0 normals"
- Fixed the QM bug where Steam hosts of Quick Matches (Player 1) would not have their chat lines sent
- EX Jaina's Phoenix Shots and EX Grave's True Dragonheart no longer incorrectly special-cancel against Long Range or Bubble Shield
- Fixed Gwen's "Gloria's Remedy" so that it doesn't draw a card or return to hand when countered, as per the FAQ
- German and Japanese text updates

notes.title: 2015-10-01 update
notes.notes:
Here are today's patch notes:

- Several new status effect icons, thanks to the community
- Fixed EX Menelker being unable to powerup for deck jokers, and fixed his discard jokers being incorrectly shown as legal to retrieve
- When you reconnect to a game you were disconnected from, the game now refills your timer up to at most one bar, as a courtesy
- Fixed Steam/iOS local games vs Yomibot not resetting knockdown state after a throw clash
- Hand moves (reordering cards in hand and flipping them) no longer need to tell the server each time, and instead are buffered locally until the next real move. This lightens the load on the server and should reduce overall network lag.
- Centered popup messages more esthetically when the sidebar chat is opened
- Allowed Gloria to pass Overdose, let the opponent Gloria Overdose, then get a second chance to play Overdose
- Upgraded the Unity engine, which should improve performance and fix a Mac issue with starting the game in fullscreen

Enjoy the game!

notes.title: 2015-08-03 update
notes.notes:
Here are today's Yomi patch notes:

- You can now buy the expansion characters through the standard Steam store page, as a DLC, in addition to buying them in-game. Both ways are equivalent.
- Fixed JP EX character card typos for Grave, Valerie, and Geiger
- Fixed typo on Gwen's reference card (all languages): Q deals 1 block damage, not 3
- Faster card stats reception from the server (much less initial standalone main menu and initial Card Collection screen stuttering)
- Fixed BBB dodging a Bubble Shielded Argagarg then being able to pump a followup Gyro Spin (for no damage)
- Fixed Quince Yomibot not saying an ability chat quote for Two Truths
- Fixed Quince Yomibot saying two ability chat quotes during Positive Spin
- Fixed some memory leaks slowing down the game over time
- Fixed EX BBB dealing no damage or block damage, and being unable to combo after a starter, against ranged BBB
- Added /clear chat command to manually delete all old chat lines
- Fixed Steam game sharing resulting in rejected Steam authentication

notes.title: 2015-07-03 update: Various fixes
notes.notes:
Today's update is simply a collection of various fixes to the game:

- Steam: Fixed chat lines and chat log list being slightly off
- Whispers now show up as in-game chat bubbles too, and display on all three chat tabs
- Player name max length 30 -> 32, to accommodate all Steam display names
- Fixed a case where the Match Chat screen became inaccessible during a local game vs AI
- Fixed the in-game menu being impossible to close when the chat is fully opened
- Steam & iOS: Fixed double KO game crash when playing offline vs bots
- Fixed typo in BBB's reference card (Overdrive is [Draw Phase], not [During Combat])
- Fixed EX Zane's A Little Shake-Up triggering when combat involves jokers
- Fixed EX Vendetta's Carrion Counter's interaction with blocked pumpable enders, and with Time Stop
- Steam: Fixed Card Collection screen showing a "Unlock 10 Expansion Characters" button when you already own the expansion
- Fixed "name_generals_armor" typo when countering General's Armor
- The tutorial opponent is now easier to defeat
- Steam Mac: Fixed corrupted application icon
- Inscribed cards: Fixed Patriot Mirror counting the first combat card as "Played in combat" for stats purposes, rather than counting the card actually kept by Quince

notes.title: Now available on Steam - Yomi, 34% off!
notes.notes:
Yomi is now available on Steam and is 34% off for the launch week! (It's already on iOS, the [URL=www.fantasystrike.com]web[/URL], and in [URL=www.sirlingames.com/collections/yomi]physical form[/URL].)

Yomi is a fighting game in card form and it's the competitive card game you should be playing. Just like in a fighting game, you have to learn your character's strengths and weaknesses, read your opponents' tendencies, and land combos when you can. Yomi is [URL=sirlin.squarespace.com/articles/game-balance-and-yomi]highly balanced[/URL] at the expert level, and it expresses the values of a [I]fair[/I] competitive game. You always have a full strength deck on an [URL=sirlin.squarespace.com/posts/sirlin-on-game-design-ep3-uneven-playfields]even playfield[/URL] with your opponents.

Yomi has [URL=www.sirlingames.com/pages/yomi-card-images]20 characters[/URL] (10 from the base game, and 10 more as an expansion), each with their own unique abilities and playstyles, leading to a whopping 210 different matchups.

Yomi is packed with features.

[LIST]
[*]Runs natively on Mac, PC, and Linux (new!)
[*]Cross-platform play with players on iOS or the web
[*]Cards have 4x the resolution as the web version!
[*]Issue challenges to people on your Steam friend list
[*]Play offline (vs bots) for the first time
[/LIST]

[IMG]http://static1.squarespace.com/static/50f14d35e4b0d70ab5fc4f24/5524bc51e4b0d62a11fbf335/5524bc55e4b026f7530fe6b7/1428470871507/YomiScreenshotNHT-CombatReveal-1280.png?format=750w[/IMG]

[IMG]http://static1.squarespace.com/static/50f14d35e4b0d70ab5fc4f24/5524bc51e4b0d62a11fbf335/5524bc57e4b0fff9d73ea5d3/1428470873054/YomiScreenshotNHT-CharSelect-1280.png?format=750w[/IMG]

[h1][B]Inscribed Cards[/B][/h1]
There's also a huge new feature called "inscribed cards." Every single Yomi card can be upgraded to an inscribed card that records your exploits! Whenever you use an inscribed card, it remembers a LOT of statistics about its fate. For example:

[LIST]
[*]How often do you hit with Dragonheart?
[*]Do your Stone Walls reflect a lot of damage?
[*]How many cards do you get with Flagstone Tax?
[*]How often do your Crash Bombs backfire?
[*]And much, much more!
[/LIST]
[IMG]http://static1.squarespace.com/static/50f14d35e4b0d70ab5fc4f24/t/5524ba31e4b0e591f7448a45/1428470322182/?format=300w[/IMG]

You can upgrade your cards even more with GOLD inscribed cards. These gold foils are sparkly and shiny. They have no gameplay advantage of course, because it wouldn't make sense to have a competitive game where some players had weaker cards, but wow are they stylish!

[IMG]http://static1.squarespace.com/static/50f14d35e4b0d70ab5fc4f24/t/5524ba3fe4b02b9e39bfaad8/1428470335833/?format=300w[/IMG]

You get inscribed cards (and occasionally gold ones!) just from playing the game. You can also buy packs of them and even scrap unwanted cards into dust that you can use to craft any particular inscribed (or gold inscribed) card that you want.

[h1][B]Even More Features[/B][/h1]
The Steam version of Yomi has some more great features that we've had in the other versions for a while now.

[LIST]
[*]Bots with two different difficulty settings
[*]An endless Survival mode
[*]A leaderboard system that lets you graduate through the student ranks, then compete in the master ranks. It gives the feeling of progression, but it's ultimately completely fair Elo behind the scenes.
[*]Save and watch replays of your games.
[*]Watch replays from any players, including the top players on the leaderboards!
[*]Powerful EX versions of all characters
[/LIST]
[IMG]http://static1.squarespace.com/static/50f14d35e4b0d70ab5fc4f24/t/5524b9b1e4b0cd08f76b538c/1428470197581/?format=750w[/IMG]
Every character has an overpowered EX version. The EX characters are not intended for competitive play, but they're really fun to mess around with. They all have new character cards with more powerful abilities, and a new rank of face cards called Destiny cards that give them a new special move of some sort. The destiny card are really flavorful too, letting each character do more of what they always wished they could. EX characters can also use the power up mechanic to get ANY cards from their deck, not just Aces.

You can play against AI that uses EX characters and you can unlock them to play in 1p modes. You can also directly buy them if you want them more quickly. We're also announcing the price of directly buying EX characters is now 80% off! They're just 99 cents rather than $5.
